correctness_confidence.basis: Sorting larger demands earlier in each stratum simultaneously minimizes all trailing contributions. The regulatory note tests the previous six months, and the monthly difference of 15 times 529.4 is 7,941 UGX.

rigor.basis: All grouped calendars retain the Q4 sequence and multiset. Positive discounts and exchangeability within strata suffice. More explicit arithmetic for the January and August witness would improve exposition.

novelty.basis: The suffix sorting argument is elementary. Its application to the archived tariff comparator, actual input precision and exact identification by number of high months is specific and verifiable.

significance.basis: A familiar annual-average comparator can mask the entire quarterly subsidy under these modeled loads. The paper cannot establish real household incidence or a reversal of the PV-versus-grid decision.

reproducibility.basis: The exact three archived load inputs, checksums, official tariff reference, two checks of the six-high panel and the full binary calendar enumeration are available. The two PDF builds match.

summary: I participated in the study and reviewed the three pages of this exact PDF. The sorted-suffix proof gives sharp bills for the specified strata and discounts, and the single busy-month counterexample is transparent. The study tests a tariff comparator against a statutory eligibility rule under synthetic demand, not actual customer billing outcomes.
strengths: Conditional discount and energy charge are separated so changes can be attributed to consumption history.
Both comparison years retain the entire monthly distribution and quarterly consumption sequence.
The source household is off-grid and the paper accurately labels its grid price counterfactual.
weaknesses: Calendar billing and stationary within-month daily shapes simplify customer behavior.
Economic incidence, connection cost, other charges and demand variation beyond two profiles are outside this experiment.
The theoretical result is a direct monotone rearrangement and does not establish broad priority.
potential_errors: Interpreting 8 of 384 groups as an empirical household probability is unwarranted.
Averaging the current month into its own eligibility test would alter the result.
Applying Q4 rates retrospectively to earlier billing periods would exceed the cited schedule.
strong_novelty_candidates: The attainable quarterly discount loss is identified for every fixed number of high-demand months despite preserving the usage distribution and billed-period loads.
